cards.front: What should you know about sustainability?
cards.back: means meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. In chemistry, this means using resources responsibly and minimising environmental impact.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sustainable Chemistry
cards.back: The reduce, reuse, recycle principles help conserve finite resources and reduce waste and environmental impact.

cards.front: What should you know about corrosion?
cards.back: is the deterioration of metals by reaction with substances in the environment. Rusting is the corrosion of iron, which requires both oxygen and water . Corrosion weakens metals and can be dangerous and expensive.

cards.front: What should you know about sacrificial protection?
cards.back: works because a more reactive metal (e.g. zinc, magnesium) will oxidise in preference to iron. The more reactive metal sacrifices itself to protect the iron.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sustainable Chemistry
cards.back: A life cycle assessment (LCA) assesses the environmental impact of a product at each stage of its life: raw materials , manufacturing , using , and disposing .

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sustainable Chemistry
cards.back: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with one or more other elements. Alloys are harder than pure metals because the different-sized atoms disrupt the regular structure, preventing layers from sliding over each other.

cards.front: What should you know about phosphate rock?
cards.back: is a finite resource used to make phosphate fertilisers. It is mined and treated with acid to make it soluble so plants can absorb the nutrients.

cards.front: What should you know about green chemistry?
cards.back: aims to reduce the environmental impact of industrial processes. This includes using renewable raw materials , reducing energy use, minimising waste, and finding cleaner reactions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sustainable Chemistry
cards.back: You need to calculate atom economy, interpret data on energy use for recycling vs extraction, and compare environmental impacts quantitatively.
